sections.markdown:
## C — The four-part driver examination: who must test, the written test, vision standards, the road sign test, the driving test, grading, retests and fraud
Knowledge domain: who has to sit the Missouri driver examination, what the written test covers, the acuity and side-vision standards, the vehicle the driving test requires, the maneuvers the Highway Patrol examiner scores, how the driving test is graded and retaken, and what counts as exam fraud.

FACT_ID: sec03-F01 | anchor: A01
The Missouri driver examination has four parts: a written test on traffic laws and safe-driving rules, a vision test, a road sign test and a driving skills test. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec03-F02 | anchor: A01
A driver whose license from another state is valid or expired less than 184 days, applying for the same type of Missouri license, takes only the vision and road sign tests. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec03-F03 | anchor: A01
The examination is required for a new Missouri license, for a Missouri license expired more than six months (184 days), and whenever the Director of Revenue asks, even if your license is current. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec03-F04 | anchor: A01
A license revoked for too many points or for an Administrative Alcohol action also sends the driver back through the examination. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec03-F05 | anchor: A01
The Missouri State Highway Patrol (MSHP) gives the driver examination, and either the MSHP or the Department can point you to the nearest testing center. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec03-F06 | anchor: A01
You must prove your legal name and age before the exam, and you show that identification again whenever you apply for a license or permit and each time you take the written or driving test. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec03-F07 | anchor: A01
The Class F written test has 25 multiple-choice questions on the laws and driving methods this guide covers. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec03-F08 | anchor: A01
The written test is not open book, and a Class F applicant is not tested on the commercial vehicle material in Chapter 15. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec03-F09 | anchor: A01
A Class E for-hire applicant takes a special written test that adds the Chapter 15 commercial vehicle material, and it is also not open book. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec03-F10 | anchor: A01
Every new or renewal license or permit applicant takes both an acuity test and a peripheral (side) vision test. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec03-F11 | anchor: A01
The standard minimum acuity is 20/40 or better using either eye or both eyes. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec03-F12 | anchor: A02
The standard minimum side vision is 55 degrees or more in each eye, or 85 degrees or more in one eye. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec03-F13 | anchor: A02
Missing the vision standards can lead to a denied license or to restrictions placed on the license. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec03-F14 | anchor: A02
If you fail the standard vision test, the examiner hands you a vision exam form for an eye specialist or physician, and a new prescription may mean waiting for the glasses or contacts before the written or driving test. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec03-F15 | anchor: A02
If both natural and corrected acuity are worse than 20/160, or combined side vision is worse than 70 degrees, you cannot take the driving test or hold a Missouri license. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec03-F16 | anchor: A02
The road sign test checks whether you can recognize traffic signs and understand what they mean. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec03-F17 | anchor: A02
The driving test comes only after the written, vision and road sign tests are passed, and it is given by an MSHP driver license examiner. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec03-F18 | anchor: A02
The examiner inspects the test vehicle for required equipment and safe condition, and the test is refused if the vehicle is not properly equipped or testing seems dangerous. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec03-F19 | anchor: A02
The test vehicle needs current plates, a valid inspection sticker, working seat belts, working doors for the driver and the examiner, and a clean, safe passenger seat. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec03-F20 | anchor: A02
The test vehicle also needs a working parking brake and foot brake, a working horn, and proof of financial responsibility. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec03-F21 | anchor: A02
Only you and the examiner ride during the test; skip needless conversation, remember the examiner is there to test rather than teach, and obey every Missouri traffic law. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec03-F22 | anchor: A02
When asked to use controls such as the accelerator, brakes, turn signals and wipers, you are graded on finding each one without searching and using it correctly. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec03-F23 | anchor: A02
When you pull away you are graded on starting the car, releasing the parking brake, checking that the way is clear, signaling, and driving smoothly at the right speed. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec03-F24 | anchor: A03
Starting and stopping are graded for smoothness and safety, reaction time and control of the car while stopping. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec03-F25 | anchor: A03
The parallel parking task uses a space 25 feet long and seven feet wide. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec03-F26 | anchor: A03
Parallel parking is scored on stopping no more than 18 inches from the curb, near the middle of the space, and finishing within two minutes. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec03-F27 | anchor: A03
Parallel parking is also scored on your position before backing, not touching the space markers, turning the wheels the right way, and checking traffic and signaling before pulling out. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec03-F28 | anchor: A03
When backing, you look over your right shoulder through the rear window and must keep a straight line, stay in the proper lane and hold the right speed. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec03-F29 | anchor: A03
You make at least two right turns and two left turns, graded on lane choice, timely signals, turning into the proper lane, traffic checks, speed and control. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec03-F30 | anchor: A03
Parking on a hill is graded on stopping no more than 18 inches from the curb, leaving the car in park or the correct gear, turning the front wheels correctly, setting the parking brake, then checking traffic and signaling. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec03-F31 | anchor: A03
At intersections you are graded on obeying signs and lights, approach speed, awareness of traffic, lane position, yielding without blocking traffic, and a full stop at the proper place for stop signs. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec03-F32 | anchor: A04
Throughout the test the examiner also watches your following distance, speed, lane use and lane markings, traffic awareness and yielding. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec03-F33 | anchor: A04
The examiner deducts points for driving errors, and losing more than 30 points fails the driving test. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec03-F34 | anchor: A04
You fail at once for an at-fault crash with another vehicle, hitting a pedestrian, driving so dangerously a crash could have resulted, breaking a traffic law, or refusing to drive as directed. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec03-F35 | anchor: A04
Passing earns a test results form, but that form is not valid for driving; you must first apply for and receive a license at a license office. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec03-F36 | anchor: A04
Only one driving test may be taken per day, and the examiner will suggest practice before a retest. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec03-F37 | anchor: A04
After three failed driving tests, no further test is allowed without written Department authorization, and you must complete extra behind-the-wheel training, send proof, and receive approval to test. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec03-F38 | anchor: A04
Fraud in any license, permit or nondriver ID examination, such as false statements, cheating, or using a recording, camera or two-way communication device, is a Class A misdemeanor that can cost your driving privilege for up to one year. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0023]

Misconceptions: the written test is not open book; a Class F applicant is not quizzed on the commercial vehicle chapter; the driving test result form does not let you drive; failing the vision screen does not end the process, because a specialist can examine you first.
Mnemonics: written, eyes, signs, drive is the order of the four-part exam; parallel and hill parking share the same curb-distance limit.
Glossary: acuity means sharpness of vision; peripheral vision means side vision measured in degrees; MSHP means the Missouri State Highway Patrol, which administers the exam; financial responsibility means proof of insurance for the test vehicle.
Dynamic facts: testing center locations and the Highway Patrol website address can change and must be refreshed from the MSHP or Department of Revenue websites.
